column1: # CONFORMANCE TABLE -- c2's inline decision function, clause by clause.
# Lane w-inlmetric. Source: docs/whitebox/ref/P_INLINE.md SS1-SS2 +
# docs/whitebox/WB_INLINE_FINDINGS.md SS1-SS2.4. Frozen by work/w-inlmetric/PREREG.md SS1.
# ADDRESS REPAIR, lane w-clausefix 2026-08-28, under work/w-clausefix/PREREG.md.
# TEN of the 24 `addr` cells did not name the instruction their `clause` names:
#   C2 C3 C4 C14 C16 C17 C18 C19  -- mid-instruction, found by the ALIGN check
#   C10 C15                       -- ALIGNED, in the right function, WRONG
#                                    instruction; no alignment check can see
#                                    this class, which is why `asm` exists.
# Only the `addr` column moved, plus the additive `asm` column. No clause, owner,
# state, witness, exercised or note cell was touched, and the split is unchanged
# at absent 17 / fitted 2 / R-derived 2 / unexercisable 3 over 24 rows
# (reachable denominator 21).
# THIS IS A PROGRESS INSTRUMENT, NEVER A GATE (docs/FUNCTION_BYTE_MATCH.md SS0).
# It licenses no emit. Nothing here enters crates/.
# addr        the c2 VA the clause is read at, in c2.dll sha256 c80981c0..a66258.
#             MECHANICALLY CHECKED by work/w-inlmetric/check_table.py, three ways:
#             (1) ADDRESS -- inside the FUNCS.tsv extent of `owner`;
#             (2) ALIGN   -- starts an instruction, per the INDEPENDENT objdump
#                            listing (not the Ghidra database the addrs came from);
#             (3) DECODE  -- the instruction there is the one `asm` records.
# owner       the function the page claims the addr is in. A mismatch is RED.
# asm         the objdump `-M intel` text at `addr`, runs of blanks collapsed.
#             It PINS THE ADDRESS TO A DECODE. It does NOT verify the clause --
#             for the four rows whose clause cites a function ENTRY (C1, C5/C6,
#             C20, C21) the witness is `push ebp`, which is weak ON PURPOSE and
#             is recorded here so nobody reads DECODE-GREEN as clause-confirmed.
# state       R-derived | fitted | absent | unexercisable
#               R-derived     the port's counterpart is derived from the same
#                             field/fact c2 tests, with a DISCLOSURE-grade trail.
#               fitted        a counterpart exists and is a black-box FIT, not
#                             a reading of this clause.
#               absent        no counterpart in crates/. Ties break HERE (PREREG SS5).
#               unexercisable no compilation this project runs can reach the
#                             clause, so `absent` would mis-read it.
# witness     path:token  (verified present)  |  none:<token-that-must-be-ABSENT>
# exercised   yes | no | not-separable | unexercisable  -- by the 878-TU workload,
#             measured on the 100-TU hold-out's 8,936 graded callees where possible.
